evidence: Hays — Natural Purola Plants lists Cephalanthus occidentalis; Hays County riparian EIS also identifies buttonbush as prominent in the riparian shrub stratum.
Travis — Balcones Canyonlands Preserve plant list and UT Travis County Rubiaceae herbarium index include Cephalanthus occidentalis.
Williamson — UT Plant Resources Center provides a detailed Williamson County treatment.

morphology.look_here_first: Start with the inflorescence and leaf arrangement. Buttonbush has distinctive spherical white flower heads with projecting styles that look like pincushions, plus opposite or whorled glossy entire leaves on a wet-site shrub.
diagnostic_traits: branches often opposite or in whorls of 3
leaves opposite or whorled, simple and entire
long projecting styles create pincushion appearance
strong association with pond margins, streams, and riparian wetlands
